title: I make almost all 3D modeling into CLO. Even if it's not clothes
content:
CLO and Marevlous Designer are programs specializing in creating costumes.

![58b4b5b12073489c921ae79b9022a5a6](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202511/2125a68a5a314e2e9b3b6ad05a8a5ba3/images/58b4b5b12073489c921ae79b9022a5a6KakaoTalk_20251010_065743436.png)Fabric simulation functions and sewing-related tools make it easy to create real clothes.  
However, there are quite a few cases when you make a costume or in the process of directing it later, you need something other than the costume. It can be a subsidiary material or a prop.  
  
It seems like there are quite a few people who make shoes and some subsidiary materials by spreading the method, but there are still quite a few people looking for other tools or platforms.  
  
Asset in the digital world is different from the real thing, whether it's a person, a building, or a garment, it's a bunch of mesh objects that have the right shape, the right size, the right color.  
  
It is not difficult to make something that is not clothes using CLO.  
Just like drawing a pattern, you draw the right shape, and you put the right material on it.  
And don't do random simulations  
  
If you're wondering if you should learn another tool for modeling, please think about it.  
  
I think it's more important how you make it, rather than what kind of tool it is.

  
Maybe we should get used to thinking about it every time we design.

![1131380e3edb4d18a9b403c85b31d8cd](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202511/2125a68a5a314e2e9b3b6ad05a8a5ba3/images/1131380e3edb4d18a9b403c85b31d8cdCap%202025-10-28%2000-30-54-232.jpg)![5bbb1cfb6f8b4741acf9d417eee0973a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202511/2125a68a5a314e2e9b3b6ad05a8a5ba3/images/5bbb1cfb6f8b4741acf9d417eee0973aCap%202025-10-28%2000-31-27-906.jpg)![11d4fde0c92a472a90f742a535e1d6ab](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202511/2125a68a5a314e2e9b3b6ad05a8a5ba3/images/11d4fde0c92a472a90f742a535e1d6abCoffee_Chocolate_Set1.png)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: That's cool:) Did you also modeled the lego figure in clo? How do you do the round corners for objects? I find it to be the most annoying and difficult part:)Also, the realistic texturing? Do you simply rely on correct texture maps or you have any tricks for that too? Thanks!
Reply 1: The Lego figure was also modeled as CLO! With proper adjustment of the thickness, curvature, and particle spacing, it can be made without difficulty.The material is completed by adjusting the detailed properties, as well as using Texture map, Normal Map, Displacement map, opacity map, roughness map, metalness map, and so on.Texture maps can be drawn and created by themselves or made using AI tools.

Comment 2: Great tip!👏 What hard surface objects have you modeled so far?
Reply 1: Thank you! From small things like chocolate and coffee to accessories like clothes and glasses to toys and buildings! I've worked on everything from unique sculptures to furniture, interior design, and exterior.

Comment 3: 😍 This is incredible!!!!👍🏻
Reply 1: Thank you for always saying good things😍
content_description: This page explores how CLO and Marvelous Designer can be used not only for costume creation but also for designing props and subsidiary materials by focusing on the design process rather than the tools themselves.

title: custom avatar measurement problem
content:

Guys what the hell. I inputed my friend's measurements into the avatar and it became quasimodo.

I tried changing the pose to no avail, it still looks like ...that  


  
The values I tweaked:  
  
Height  
  
Across shoulder(Curveliniar) <this one is the biggest oof but others still make it weird  
  
Chest circumference  
Thigh circumference  
High hip circumference  
Low hip circumference  
Neck base circumference  
Waist circumference  
  
High hip height  
  
Total rise  
  
Vertical trunk  
  


Any help would be appreciated because holy fuck

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: I've found that it is important to start with a size that is simillar to the size im trying to adjust to, ideally within 4cm + or - of my custom meausurments. Try to see what size is closet to you friends measurments firstThen drop that size on your avatar and open the editorStart with the Total height and which ever measurment is to the left of it (Bust usually) Then work you way down each adjustemnt from top of list to the bottom
